regen_doc:
A File Gateway requires access to upload files into the Amazon S3 bucket, and to perform actions on any access points or VPC endpoints it uses to connect to the bucket. To obtain this access, the File Gateway assumes an IAM role. The role is associated with an IAM policy that grants the access, and the policy determines which actions the role can perform. The role also has a security token service (STS) trust relationship. The example trust policy allows the storagegateway.amazonaws.com service principal to perform sts:AssumeRole.

For the role to work, the S3 bucket must have an access policy that allows the IAM role to access it. Likewise, any associated access points or VPC endpoints must have an access policy that allows the IAM role to access them.

You can create the role and access policy yourself, or the File Gateway can create them for you. A policy created by the File Gateway contains a list of S3 actions. Storage Gateway can also assume existing service roles that are passed using the iam:PassRole policy action. However, Storage Gateway does not support IAM policies that use the iam:PassedToService context key to limit the action to specific services.

If you do not want the File Gateway to create a policy on your behalf, you create your own policy and attach it to the file share. In the example bucket policy, the first statement allows bucket-level S3 actions on the bucket amzn-s3-demo-bucket, and the second statement allows object-level S3 actions on all objects in amzn-s3-demo-bucket.

The access point example policy allows the File Gateway to perform object actions through an access point. If you need to connect the file share to an S3 bucket through a VPC endpoint, note that endpoint policies for Amazon S3 are described in the AWS PrivateLink User Guide.

Finally, if the S3 bucket is encrypted, the file share must use the key in the destination S3 bucket account.

repair.regen_doc:
# Granting a File Gateway access to an Amazon S3 bucket

## Before you begin

Set up the following before you configure the gateway's access.

- **S3 bucket (and any access points or VPC endpoints) with an access policy that allows the IAM role to access it.** The bucket's access policy, and the access policy of any associated access points or VPC endpoints, must allow the IAM role to access them. Example policies appear later on this page.
- **IAM role that the File Gateway assumes, with a security token service (STS) trust relationship.** You can create the role yourself, or the File Gateway can create it for you. For steps to create the role, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_create_for-service.html.
- **IAM identity policy granting the role the needed S3 actions** on the bucket and objects, or through an access point. The steps are on this page, in the sections below.
- **VPC endpoint policy allowing access to S3**, needed only if you connect through a VPC endpoint. For steps, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html.

## How access works

A File Gateway requires access to upload files into the Amazon S3 bucket. It also requires access to perform actions on any access points or VPC endpoints it uses to connect to the bucket. To obtain this access, the File Gateway assumes an IAM role.

The role assumption works only when all of the following hold: the role is associated with an IAM policy that grants the access, the role has an STS trust relationship, the S3 bucket has an access policy that allows the IAM role to access it, and any associated access points or VPC endpoints have an access policy that allows the IAM role to access them. The IAM policy determines which actions the role can perform.

You can create the role and access policy yourself, or the File Gateway can create them for you. If the File Gateway creates them, the policy it creates contains a list of S3 actions.

## The trust policy

The example trust policy allows the storagegateway.amazonaws.com service principal to perform sts:AssumeRole. A trust policy like this is enough for the File Gateway to assume the role.

Storage Gateway can also assume existing service roles that are passed using the iam:PassRole policy action. Storage Gateway does not support IAM policies that use the iam:PassedToService context key to limit the action to specific services.

## Using your own policy

If you do not want the File Gateway to create a policy on your behalf, create your own policy and attach it to the file share.

## Example bucket policy

The first statement of the example bucket policy allows bucket-level S3 actions on the bucket amzn-s3-demo-bucket. The second statement allows object-level S3 actions on all objects in amzn-s3-demo-bucket.

## Example access point policy

The access point example policy allows the File Gateway to perform object actions through an access point.

## Connecting through a VPC endpoint

If you need to connect the file share to an S3 bucket through a VPC endpoint, see the endpoint policies for Amazon S3 described in the AWS PrivateLink User Guide.

## Encrypted buckets

If the S3 bucket is encrypted, the file share must use the key in the destination S3 bucket account.

A File Gateway requires access to upload files into the Amazon S3 bucket, and it also requires access to perform actions on any access points or VPC endpoints it uses to connect to the bucket. To obtain this access, the File Gateway assumes an IAM role. The role is associated with an IAM policy that grants the access, and the policy determines which actions the role can perform. The role also has a security token service (STS) trust relationship. The example trust policy allows the storagegateway.amazonaws.com service principal to perform sts:AssumeRole.

For the role to work, the S3 bucket must have an access policy that allows the IAM role to access it. Likewise, any associated access points or VPC endpoints must have an access policy that allows the IAM role to access them.

You can create the role and access policy yourself, or the File Gateway can create them for you. A policy created by the File Gateway contains a list of S3 actions. Storage Gateway can also assume existing service roles passed using the iam:PassRole policy action. However, Storage Gateway does not support IAM policies that use the iam:PassedToService context key to limit the action to specific services.

If you do not want the File Gateway to create a policy on your behalf, you create your own policy and attach it to the file share. In the example bucket policy, the first statement allows bucket-level S3 actions on the bucket amzn-s3-demo-bucket, and the second statement allows object-level S3 actions on all objects in amzn-s3-demo-bucket.

The access point example policy allows the File Gateway to perform object actions through an access point. If you need to connect the file share to an S3 bucket through a VPC endpoint, note that endpoint policies for Amazon S3 are described in the AWS PrivateLink User Guide.

If the S3 bucket is encrypted, the file share must use the key in the destination S3 bucket account.

repair.regen_doc:
# Granting a File Gateway access to an Amazon S3 bucket

## Before you begin

Have the following in place before you configure access. Each item is needed by a step later on this page.

- An IAM role that the File Gateway can assume, with a security token service (STS) trust relationship (a trust policy). The steps are on this page.
- An IAM identity policy attached to that role, granting the S3 actions on the bucket and its objects (or on the access point). The steps are on this page.
- An access policy on the S3 bucket, and on any associated access points or VPC endpoints, that allows the IAM role to access them.
- A VPC endpoint policy for S3, if you connect the file share through a VPC endpoint. The steps are at https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html.

## How access works

A File Gateway requires access to upload files into the Amazon S3 bucket. It also requires access to perform actions on any access points or VPC endpoints it uses to connect to the bucket. To obtain this access, the File Gateway assumes an IAM role.

The role is associated with an IAM policy that grants the access, and the IAM policy determines which actions the role can perform. The role also has an STS trust relationship. The File Gateway can assume the role only when both the IAM policy and the STS trust relationship are in place. The S3 bucket must also have an access policy that allows the IAM role to access it, and any associated access points or VPC endpoints must have an access policy that allows the role to access them. The File Gateway can assume the role only when these access policies are also in place, in addition to the IAM policy and trust relationship.

You can create the role and access policy yourself, or the File Gateway can create them for you. A policy created by the File Gateway contains a list of S3 actions.

## Trust policy

The example trust policy allows the `storagegateway.amazonaws.com` service principal to perform `sts:AssumeRole`. With this trust policy in place, the File Gateway can assume the role.

Storage Gateway can also assume existing service roles that are passed using the `iam:PassRole` policy action. Storage Gateway does not support IAM policies that use the `iam:PassedToService` context key to limit the action to specific services.

## Creating your own policy

If you do not want the File Gateway to create a policy on your behalf, you create your own policy and attach it to the file share.

## Example bucket policy

The first statement of the example bucket policy allows bucket-level S3 actions on the bucket `amzn-s3-demo-bucket`. The second statement allows object-level S3 actions on all objects in `amzn-s3-demo-bucket`.

## Example access point policy

The access point example policy allows the File Gateway to perform object actions through an access point.

## Connecting through a VPC endpoint

If you need to connect the file share to an S3 bucket through a VPC endpoint, configure a VPC endpoint policy for S3. Endpoint policies for Amazon S3 are described in the AWS PrivateLink User Guide.

## Encrypted buckets

If the S3 bucket is encrypted, the file share must use the key in the destination S3 bucket account.
